// ===== Ordering/OpenOrders.cs =====
// Generated by `write-specs` (WolverineFx.Bobcat.EventModel) from the model's examples. Nothing regenerates it.

namespace Orders.Specs.Ordering;

[BobcatFeature("OpenOrders")]
[BobcatSlice(SliceType = typeof(OpenOrders))]
public class open_orders(AppFixture app) : OrdersHttpSpec(app)
{
    [Fact]
    public async Task lists_the_open_orders()
    {
        var theOrder = Guid.CreateVersion7(); // "o-1" in the model

        await GivenEvents<Order>(theOrder, Specify<OrderPlaced>().With(x => x.OrderId, theOrder).Tagged(theOrder));

        await ThenDocuments<OpenOrders>(Expect.InAnyOrder(Specify<OpenOrders>()
            .With(x => x.OrderId, theOrder)
            .With(x => x.Total, 1500m)));
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task no_open_orders_at_the_start()
    {
        await ThenNoReadModel<OpenOrders>();
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task asked_for_one_customer()
    {
        var theCustomer = Guid.CreateVersion7(); // "c-9" in the model
        var theOrder = Guid.CreateVersion7();

        await GivenEvents<Order>(theOrder, Specify<OrderPlaced>().With(x => x.OrderId, theOrder));

        // The board gives the OpenOrders query no route, so this is the one scaffold writes for it
        var response = await WhenReading<OpenOrders>("/api/open-orders/{customerId}", theCustomer);

        await ThenReadModel<OpenOrders>(theCustomer, Specify<OpenOrders>().With(x => x.Total, 1500m));
    }
}

// ===== Ordering/PlaceOrder.cs =====
// Generated by `write-specs` (WolverineFx.Bobcat.EventModel) from the model's examples. Nothing regenerates it.

namespace Orders.Specs.Ordering;

// An order needs at least one line.
// Orders over 1000 need approval.
[BobcatFeature("PlaceOrder")]
[BobcatSlice(SliceType = typeof(PlaceOrder))]
public class place_order(AppFixture app) : OrdersSpec(app)
{
    // Blocked on the board, so the specification is pending until the slice is ready
    [BobcatSpec(Pending = true)]
    public async Task places_an_order_over_the_approval_limit()
    {
        // Approval is a manual step outside the system.
        // Acted by Customer

        var theOrder = Guid.CreateVersion7(); // "o-1" in the model

        await GivenReadModel<ApprovalLimits>(Specify<ApprovalLimits>()
            .With(x => x.Id, theOrder)
            .With(x => x.Limit, 1000));
        await GivenNoEventsFor<Order>(theOrder);

        await WhenReceived(Specify<PlaceOrder>().With(x => x.OrderId, theOrder).With(x => x.Total, 1500m));

        // PlacedAt is generated by the handler, so the example's value is not compared
        ThenEvents(Specify<OrderPlaced>().With(x => x.OrderId, theOrder).With(x => x.Total, 1500m).Tagged(theOrder));
    }

    // Blocked on the board, so the specification is pending until the slice is ready
    [BobcatSpec(Pending = true)]
    public async Task refuses_an_empty_order()
    {
        // Acted by Customer

        var theOrder = Guid.CreateVersion7(); // "o-2" in the model

        await WhenReceived(Specify<PlaceOrder>().With(x => x.OrderId, theOrder).With(x => x.Total, 0m));

        ThenRefusedWith("An order needs at least one line");
        ThenNoEvents();
    }
}

// ===== Ordering/SendConfirmation.cs =====
// Generated by `write-specs` (WolverineFx.Bobcat.EventModel) from the model's examples. Nothing regenerates it.

namespace Orders.Specs.Ordering;

// The confirmation is a courtesy; the order stands without it.
// SendConfirmation is an automation, triggered by "Order Placed Processor"
[BobcatFeature("SendConfirmation")]
[BobcatSlice(SliceType = typeof(SendConfirmation))]
public class send_confirmation(AppFixture app) : OrdersSpec(app)
{
    // Informational on the board: it documents the slice rather than specifying it, so it is pending
    [BobcatSpec(Pending = true)]
    public async Task confirms_a_placed_order()
    {
        var theOrder = Guid.CreateVersion7(); // "o-1" in the model

        await GivenEvents<Order>(theOrder, Specify<OrderPlaced>().With(x => x.OrderId, theOrder).Tagged(theOrder));

        await WhenReceived(Specify<SendConfirmation>().With(x => x.OrderId, theOrder));

        ThenEvents(Specify<ConfirmationSent>().With(x => x.OrderId, theOrder));
    }
}

// ===== TestSupport.cs =====
// Generated by `write-specs` (WolverineFx.Bobcat.EventModel). Nothing regenerates this file.

using Alba;
using Marten;
using Wolverine;

namespace Orders.Specs;

/// <summary>
/// The application under test: its own host, configured as it is in production and started once for
/// every specification. Alba needs the application's Program to be public, so the application
/// declares <c>public partial class Program;</c>.
/// </summary>
/// <remarks>
/// The specifications use the application's own database and schema, so the data a failing
/// specification leaves behind is where a developer would look for it.
/// </remarks>
public class AppFixture : IAsyncLifetime
{
    public IAlbaHost Host { get; private set; } = null!;

    public async ValueTask InitializeAsync()
        => Host = await AlbaHost.For<Program>(x => x.ConfigureServices(services =>
        {
            services.DisableAllExternalWolverineTransports();
            services.RunWolverineInSoloMode();

            // Marten's async daemon, in solo mode so projections run in this process
            services.MartenDaemonModeIsSolo();

            // Under xUnit v3 the test project is the entry assembly, which Wolverine would otherwise
            // adopt as the application assembly, and then find no handlers or endpoints in
            services.ConfigureWolverine(opts => opts.ApplicationAssembly = typeof(Program).Assembly);
        }));

    public async ValueTask DisposeAsync() => await Host.DisposeAsync();
}

/// <summary>
/// Every specification shares the one host and runs one at a time, because each resets the event store.
/// </summary>
[CollectionDefinition("Orders")]
public class OrdersCollection : ICollectionFixture<AppFixture>;

/// <summary>
/// The base of every specification: the Given/When/Then vocabulary, and a reset before each test.
/// ResetAsync resets every event store the host registers (Marten, Polecat or Fisher), so each
/// specification starts from an empty store. Nothing is torn down afterwards, on purpose.
/// </summary>
[Collection("Orders")]
public abstract class OrdersSpec(AppFixture app) : WolverineSpec(app.Host), IAsyncLifetime
{
    public async ValueTask InitializeAsync() => await ResetAsync();

    public ValueTask DisposeAsync() => ValueTask.CompletedTask;
}

/// <summary>
/// The base of a specification whose act is an HTTP request or a query: the same host through Alba, with
/// WhenPosted, WhenReading and the response assertions of WolverineFx.Bobcat.Http, and the same reset.
/// </summary>
[Collection("Orders")]
public abstract class OrdersHttpSpec(AppFixture app) : WolverineHttpSpec(app.Host), IAsyncLifetime
{
    public async ValueTask InitializeAsync() => await ResetAsync();

    public ValueTask DisposeAsync() => ValueTask.CompletedTask;
}
